text: Woe to those who devise iniquity, who work out evil on their beds! At dawn they carry it out, because they have the power to do it.

versions.text: Woe to those who plot evil, who plan wickedness on their beds! At dawn they carry it out, because they have the power to do it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pairs two different actions: חֹשְׁבֵי־אָוֶן ("devise iniquity") and פֹּעֲלֵי רָע ("work/do evil"). The current rendering makes both verbs mean essentially "plan," losing the second element and creating a redundant doublet.

text: They covet fields and seize them, houses too, and take them away. They oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.

Therefore this is what the LORD says: See, I am planning disaster against this family, and you will not slip your necks out of it. You will no longer walk with your heads held high, for it will be a time of disaster.

On that day they will taunt you with this saying, and wail this bitter lament: "We are utterly ruined! He exchanges the portion of my people; he takes it away from me and parcels out our fields to the traitor."

versions.text: On that day they will taunt you with this saying, and wail this bitter lament: "We are utterly ruined! He has divided up my people's land; he takes it from me and parcels out our fields to the traitor."
versions.explanation: יָמִיר means "he changes/exchanges (hands)," not "divides up." As currently worded it also duplicates "parcels out" later in the same verse; "exchanges the portion" preserves the distinct image of ownership being transferred.

text: Therefore you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to cast the measuring line for an allotment.
"Stop preaching!" they preach. "Do not preach about such things; disgrace will never overtake us."
Should this be said, house of Jacob? Is the Spirit of the LORD short of patience? Are these his doings? Do my words not bring good to the one who walks uprightly?
But lately you have risen up against my people as an enemy. You strip the robe from those who pass by in peace, from those returning from war.
You drive the women of my people from their pleasant homes; you take away my glory from their children forever.
Get up and go, for this is no place of rest! Because it is defiled, it brings ruin—a grievous ruin.
If a man full of wind and falsehood should lie and say, "I will preach to you of wine and strong drink," he would be just the preacher for this people!
I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely bring together the remnant of Israel. I will place them like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture—a noisy throng of people.

versions.text: I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely bring together the remnant of Israel. I will place them like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture—the place will hum with people.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb has the flock as its subject ("they will be noisy with people"), not "the place." A rendering that keeps the flock imagery avoids introducing a subject not present in the text and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: The one who breaks open the way goes up before them; they break through the gate and pass out through it. Their king passes on before them, and the LORD at their head.
